circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, designed by Hermann Tilke, is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi that has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix annually since 2009. As the second Middle Eastern Grand Prix venue after Bahrain, it preceded the later introductions of racing events in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a Melbourne street track that loops around Albert Park Lake and hosts the annual Australian Grand Prix as its premier motorsport event, along with supporting racing series and lower categories. The venue holds the highest FIA classification for circuit safety and infrastructure.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras: initially as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, and later following its renovation and renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. Following its debut as host of the 2016 European Grand Prix, the circuit became home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the Middle East's debut as a Formula One venue. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series and 24-hour endurance racing, with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the 4. 657 km Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya features a versatile layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and machine capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and competing in the inaugural F1 season in 1950. The track has maintained an annual Grand Prix presence since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its role in top-tier motorsport, the track has accommodated various racing series including sports car championships and North American touring competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit serves as China's primary Formula One venue, hosting the Chinese Grand Prix across two periods: 2004-2019 and resuming from 2024. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing series events alongside its flagship Grand Prix.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit has served as the venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing the British Grand Prix hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch through the 1950s to 1980s, the circuit became the permanent home of the event from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the 4. 381 km Hungaroring hosted Formula One's first race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, constructed in just eight months, a record for circuit-building speed. Built outside the city near a major highway rather than in Budapest's largest park as initially considered, the venue held its inaugural grand prix on 24 March 1986 as a tribute to Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. The venue hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" for its demanding combination of extended straights and fast-paced corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km facility situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan and managed by Honda Mobilityland, serves as a premier venue for international motorsport competitions. With a spectator capacity of 155,000, the track is particularly renowned for hosting Formula One grands prix and Japanese Super Formula races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, featuring the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track passes by iconic casinos and entertainment venues such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the modern MSG Sphere structure.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, a 4. 304 km circuit, honours two tragically deceased Mexican racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez. The venue returned to the Formula One calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, hosting the Mexican Grand Prix on its current layout, which differs from the configuration used during its previous hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile circuit with 19 corners designed to accommodate qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Built by specialist track designers Apex Circuit Design, the venue was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour area. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, the track is widely known as "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix when it rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021. The partnership between the track and Formula One concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing facility positioned north of Doha, featuring a 5. 419-kilometer layout with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and an FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, officially the Autódromo José Carlos Pace, is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940. Named in 1985 after deceased Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, the counterclockwise track has hosted numerous Grand Prix events and features an adjacent kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street course positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its debut in 2021. The venue additionally began accommodating a Formula E event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a street-based racing layout that circles Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 km and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license, the venue accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside MotoGP and endurance racing events. The track has also accommodated various other major motorsport series including IndyCar and sports car championships throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver competing in Formula One for Williams under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championship titles during his 2005-2006 campaign with Renault and accumulated 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has secured six Formula One victories since joining Mercedes at the start of the 2025 season.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One driving for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as part of the Audi team. His full name is Gabriel Lourenzo Oliveira, though he is professionally known by his shorter surname Bortoleto.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning over a decade. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his Mercedes years and has secured 10 race victories across his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One as a member of the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while competing in European Le Mans Series prototype racing for Nielsen Racing. He has made seven Formula One starts across the 2024-2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The Frenchman previously achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a Franco-Algerian driver, races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond single-seaters, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, most notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished as runner-up in the 2022 drivers' championship and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW's factory team at WRT, also races part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series for Trackhouse Racing. He previously competed in Formula One across two separate stints, from 2014 to 2020 and then again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship during his eighth season in the sport. He has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his career with the Woking-based team.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The talented driver achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 world championship standings while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri represents McLaren in Formula One, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories throughout his career. Known by his "Honey Badger" moniker, he established himself as a consistent competitor in the sport before his retirement.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British competitor in Formula One, drives for Mercedes and has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 class for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 prototypes in the IMSA series.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the world championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One career spanning from 2021 through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with the Cadillac team. He currently holds this supporting position within the sport's top tier.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced as Alpine since 2021, continuing Renault's factory presence in Formula One until the manufacturer's departure in 2025. Originally known as Renault F1 Team, the squad secured its only Alpine-era victory through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix and currently competes with Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations as a British manufacturer, with the present iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, has been a constant presence in Formula One since the championship's inception in 1950, establishing itself as both the longest-tenured and most accomplished team in the sport's history. The squad, colloquially referred to as "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains the only organization to have participated in every World Championship season.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed racing outfit, founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, entered Formula One competition in 2016. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had overseen the team since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport engineering firm founded in 1970, the organization initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent constructor, achieving notable success including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours. The team competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards, establishing itself as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors before concluding operations in 2025, with Audi subsequently acquiring the team's assets to establish its own F1 entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing competes in Formula One as a British outfit headquartered in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One continuously since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is headquartered in Brackley and races under a German licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff since 2022. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's secondary entry into the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor competing since 2024 as one of two teams under Red Bull's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a second Red Bull-affiliated entry on the grid.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and became one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams in the sport. Christian Horner led the team from its inception through 2024, after which Laurent Mekies assumed the principal role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from the remnants of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team designation and operates as both constructor and competitor on the grid.
